messages:
Alex P.: hey team, first day here. got the sandbox key in my welcome email but i need a hosted/dev API key to run longer streaming tests locally. where should i get one and how do i avoid 429s during small load experiments?

Maya: welcome Alex :tada: Hosted keys are generated in Console -> API Keys. Sandbox creds are the temporary ones from the email with limited credits. If you don't see "Create API key" ping #eng-platform 1 they can adjust roles. Hosted keys are billable.

InfraBot: FYI creating hosted keys will create an audit log entry.

Sam: streaming 429s usually mean hitting concurrency or token-rate caps. best practices: reuse a persistent stream (don't open thousands of short connections), add exponential backoff + jitter on 429s, and keep client-side token accounting.

Alex P.: is there a CLI to script key creation on linux?

Maya: there is an internal helper `rci-cli`. example:
```
redwood keys create --type hosted --name "alex-autocomplete-dev"
```
It requires SSO. If you get 403, file a note in #eng-platform and they'll either create the key or fix permissions.

Lisa: also throttle client-side and use random jitter so retries don't sync. reuse connections where possible to cut handshake overhead.

Alex P.: sandbox sounds pretty tight for streaming. can i request a temporary quota bump for a focused test?

Sam: yes, we do temporary dev grants (24-72h). request format in #eng-platform: project, billing owner, start/end (UTC), estimated peak tokens/min, expected concurrency.

Maya: example request body to paste in the channel:
- project: autocomplete-playground
- billing owner: @Jordan
- window: 2026-03-30T18:00Z -> 2026-03-30T20:00Z
- peak tokens/min: ~4167 (500k total over 2h)
- concurrency: ~30 streams

eng-platform: acknowledged. please include the billing owner and exact test times. we'll review capacity and respond within one business day; temporary grants may have caps.

Alex P.: added @Jordan for billing. thanks everyone!

Jordan: acked, i'll approve billing side once eng-platform posts details.

Maya: pro tip: for streaming experiments prefer a single websocket and multiplex messages rather than many sockets. cuts down on both handshakes and likelihood of 429s.

Sam: instrument tokens/min client-side so you can proactively throttle before infra does. saves headaches.
